about: What NASA says about the rockets that could carry the rover, five of the rock samples Perseverance has sealed, and the real events behind the rover tasks. Built by scripts/fetch-rover-tasks.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
how: Each fact keeps the exact words of its source (quote) beside our short version (text or value). "by script": the script downloaded the source on the retrieval date and found the quote in it. "by hand": the script could not read the source on that run (a PDF without pdftotext, or a page drawn by a script), so the quote or figure stands as it was checked when it was added.
limits: The pictures are the ones NASA's catalog prints beside each sample: they show the drill hole and its surroundings, not the core tube. These are descriptions and a few headline figures, not a performance dataset. The Atlas V cost is NASA's 2016 figure for the whole Mars 2020 launch, not a list price. The Falcon 9 cost is for a different mission (IMAP) and stands in for a launch NASA has never bought. NASA's press kit gives no launch mass for the Mars 2020 spacecraft on its own, so that figure is our sum of two NASA numbers. NASA's sample catalog gives each sample's type, rock, dates and core length; it does not describe colour or layering. The Atacama rock stuck to Curiosity's drill, not to a wheel.
model: Our model, not NASA data: prices in credits (one credit for each $10 million of the cost figure), the success rate of each rocket, the Mars days a failed launch costs, how often the rover gets stuck, the telemetry and the fixes in the rescue, wheel wear and its effect on speed, the scan read-outs of each rock and its science value.

brief.label: Record
brief.text: The rocket that really launched both rovers: Curiosity in 2011 and Perseverance in 2020.

backing.quote: Type: Atlas V 541

source.title: Mars Science Laboratory Launch Press Kit

backing.quote: NASA began a historic voyage to Mars with the Nov. 26 launch of the Mars Science Laboratory, which carries a car-sized rover named Curiosity.

source.title: NASA Launches Most Capable and Robust Rover to Mars

backing.quote: A United Launch Alliance Atlas V 541 rocket lifts off from Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida on July 30, 2020

source.title: Mars 2020 Liftoff

brief.label: Name
brief.text: 541 stands for a 5-metre nose cone, 4 solid boosters and 1 engine on the upper stage.

backing.quote: The numbers "541" in the launch vehicle's designation signify a 5-meter (17-foot) short payload fairing, four solid-rocket boosters, and a one-engine Centaur upper stage.

source.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit: Mission Overview

backing.quote: NASA began a historic voyage to Mars with the Nov. 26 launch of the Mars Science Laboratory, which carries a car-sized rover named Curiosity.

cost.basis: NASA's total cost to launch Mars 2020 (Perseverance) on this rocket.

backing.quote: The total cost for NASA to launch Mars 2020 is approximately $243 million, which includes: the launch service; spacecraft and spacecraft power source processing; planetary protection processing; launch vehicle integration; and tracking, data and telemetry support.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for Mars 2020 Rover Mission

brief.label: Record
brief.text: NASA flies science missions on Falcon 9, among them DART and IMAP. No rover has gone to Mars on one.

backing.quote: The DART mission currently is targeted to launch in June 2021 on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 4E at Vandenberg Air Force Base in California.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for Asteroid Redirect Test Mission

backing.quote: The IMAP mission is targeted to launch in October 2024 on a Falcon 9 Full Thrust rocket from Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for IMAP Mission

backing.quote: The total cost for NASA to launch DART is approximately $69 million, which includes the launch service and other mission related costs.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for Asteroid Redirect Test Mission

backing.quote: The total cost for NASA to launch IMAP and the secondary payloads is approximately $109.4 million, which includes the launch service and other mission related costs.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for IMAP Mission

cost.basis: NASA's cost to launch IMAP on a Falcon 9, the dearer of the two Falcon 9 launches recorded here. NASA has published no price for a Falcon 9 that gives up its booster to reach Mars, so the game uses this figure as a stand-in.

backing.quote: The total cost for NASA to launch IMAP and the secondary payloads is approximately $109.4 million, which includes the launch service and other mission related costs.

source.title: NASA Awards Launch Services Contract for IMAP Mission

curiosity.text: The whole spacecraft at launch: the 899 kg rover, its landing system and the cruise stage.

backing.quote: Mass: 8,463 pounds (3,893 kilograms) total at launch, consisting of 1,982-pound (899-kilogram) rover; 5,293-pound (2,401-kilogram) entry, descent and landing system (aeroshell plus fueled descent stage); and 1,188-pound (539-kilogram) fueled cruise stage

source.title: Mars Science Laboratory Launch Press Kit

perseverance.text: NASA's press kit gives no launch mass for the Mars 2020 spacecraft on its own. It says the rover is 126 kg heavier than Curiosity, so the game adds that to Curiosity's 3,893 kg: about 4,019 kg. That sum is our estimate, not a NASA figure.

backing.quote: Perseverance has about 5 inches (3 centimeters) additional chassis length and 278 additional pounds (126 kilograms) compared to Curiosity.

source.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit

falconMarsPayload.note: What SpaceX lists as the payload a Falcon 9 can send to Mars. It applies to a booster that is not flown back and landed. Not a NASA figure. The page is drawn by a script, so the snapshot script cannot check it.

story.label: What happened
story.text: The first coring attempt. The rock crumbled to powder, so the tube was sealed with no rock in it. The catalog lists it as a sample of the air.

backing.quote: Data sent to Earth by NASA's Perseverance rover after its first attempt to collect a rock sample on Mars and seal it in a sample tube indicate that no rock was collected during the initial sampling activity.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Team Assessing First Mars Sampling Attempt

backing.quote: breaking into powder and fragments of material too small to be retained in the sample tube before it was sealed and stored within the rover.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Plans Next Sample Attempt

story.label: The rock
story.text: Basaltic rock, probably from a lava flow. Volcanic rock can be dated precisely.

backing.quote: The rock that provided the mission's first core samples is basaltic in composition and may be the product of lava flows.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Collects Puzzle Pieces of Mars' History

backing.quote: The volcanic origin of the rock could help scientists accurately date when it formed.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Collects Puzzle Pieces of Mars' History

story.label: Water
story.text: Salts in it show that water once moved through or over the rock.

backing.quote: What's more, salts have been spied within these rocks.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Collects Puzzle Pieces of Mars' History

story.text: A sandstone from the river delta, carrying grains and rock fragments that came from far outside Jezero Crater.

story.label: The rock
story.text: A mudstone: mud and fine sand that settled in an evaporating salt lake billions of years ago.

backing.quote: "Wildcat Ridge" is the name given to a rock about 3 feet (1 meter) wide that likely formed billions of years ago as mud and fine sand settled in an evaporating saltwater lake.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain

story.label: Organics
story.text: The SHERLOC instrument found organic molecules together with sulfate minerals: the most abundant organic detections of the mission at that time.

backing.quote: SHERLOC's analysis indicates the samples feature a class of organic molecules that are spatially correlated with those of sulfate minerals.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain

backing.quote: In its analysis of Wildcat Ridge, the SHERLOC instrument registered the most abundant organic detections on the mission to date.

source.title: NASA's Perseverance Rover Investigates Geologically Rich Mars Terrain

story.label: The rock
story.text: A reddish rock covered in "leopard spots".

backing.quote: NASA's Perseverance rover discovered leopard spots on a reddish rock nicknamed "Cheyava Falls" in Mars' Jezero Crater in July 2024.

source.title: NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year

story.label: Why it matters
story.text: NASA says the sample contains potential biosignatures: something that might have a biological origin but needs more study before anyone can say.

backing.quote: Taken from a rock named "Cheyava Falls" last year, the sample, called "Sapphire Canyon," contains potential biosignatures, according to a paper published Wednesday in the journal Nature.

source.title: NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year

backing.quote: A potential biosignature is a substance or structure that might have a biological origin but requires more data or further study before a conclusion can be reached about the absence or presence of life.

source.title: NASA Says Mars Rover Discovered Potential Biosignature Last Year

cards.title: Curiosity's rock delay
cards.text: In April 2026 a 13 kg (28.6 lb) rock called Atacama lifted out of the ground, stuck to Curiosity's drill. It took the team from 25 April to 1 May to shake it off.

backing.quote: On April 25, 2026, Curiosity drilled a sample from a rock nicknamed "Atacama," which is an estimated 1.5 feet in diameter at its base, 6 inches thick and weighs roughly 28.6 pounds (13 kilograms).

source.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Frees Its Drill From a Rock (PIA26723)

backing.quote: When the rover retracted its arm, the entire rock lifted out of the ground, suspended by the fixed sleeve that surrounds the rotating drill bit.

source.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Frees Its Drill From a Rock (PIA26723)

backing.quote: Finally, on May 1, Curiosity's team tried again, tilting the drill more, rotating and vibrating the drill, and spinning the drill bit.

source.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Frees Its Drill From a Rock (PIA26723)

cards.title: Worn wheels
cards.text: Curiosity's wheels began to show wear in 2013. Software now adjusts each wheel's speed to take pressure off them.

backing.quote: Even before 2013, when the wheels began to show signs of wear, JPL engineers had been studying how to reduce the effects of the rugged Martian surface.

source.title: An Algorithm Helps Protect Mars Curiosity's Wheels

backing.quote: The traction control algorithm uses real-time data to adjust each wheel's speed, reducing pressure from the rocks.

source.title: An Algorithm Helps Protect Mars Curiosity's Wheels

cards.title: A rover that really got stuck
cards.text: In 2005 Opportunity sank to its wheel rims in a small dune. Freeing it took nearly five weeks: 192 m of wheel turns to move 1 m.

backing.quote: From about 174 million kilometers away (about 108 million miles), the rover team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, Calif., had worked diligently for nearly five weeks to extricate the rover.

source.title: NASA's Opportunity Rover Rolls Free on Mars

backing.quote: In the weeks following, the rover churned 192 meters (629 feet) worth of wheel rotations before gaining enough traction to actually move one meter (about three feet).

source.title: NASA's Opportunity Rover Rolls Free on Mars

cards.title: Sample caching
cards.text: Perseverance brought 43 tubes to Mars, 38 of them for samples, and has sealed 30. One of its main goals is the search for signs of ancient microbial life.

backing.quote: Of the 43 tubes Perseverance brought to Mars, 38 are for collecting samples

source.title: Mars Rock Samples
source.provider: NASA Science, Mars 2020 Perseverance sample catalog

backing.quote: Samples Collected 30 of 38

source.title: Mars Rock Samples
source.provider: NASA Science, Mars 2020 Perseverance sample catalog

backing.quote: A key objective for Perseverance's mission on Mars is astrobiology, including the search for signs of ancient microbial life.

source.title: Meet the Mars Samples: Sapphire Canyon (Sample 25)

cards.title: Curiosity carries no tubes
cards.text: Curiosity grinds rock to powder and studies it in its own laboratory. Perseverance cuts whole cores and seals them in tubes.

backing.quote: The drill will cut intact rock cores, and they'll be placed in sample tubes via a complex storage system.

source.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit

backing.quote: (Curiosity, on the other hand, pulverizes rock for its instruments to study.)

source.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit

cards.title: Will the tubes come home?
cards.text: The mission meant to bring the tubes to Earth, Mars Sample Return, was left without funding in the United States budget passed in January 2026.

backing.quote: US Congress has rejected plans to slash NASA's science budget, restoring most funding with one notable exception: Mars Sample Return remains cancelled.

source.title: Congress throws NASA a lifeline, leaves Mars sample mission to die in the dust
source.provider: The Register (news report, not NASA), 16 January 2026
